name: Public Institutions in India: Theory and Practice
description: This course will familiarize students with India’s major public institutions, particularly those related to government and public policy, and roles they play. Students will learn about form and function of institutions, how new institutions have been designed, how their public relevance rises and falls, and their de jure and de facto operations. Students will also become familiar with institutional analysis as a methodological approach, as well as elements of public choice theory applied to these institutions and the people who run them. This will help students develop more nuanced understandings of how bureaucracies function, their interactions with citizens, and how the compact between public institutions and citizens has evolved. Specific cases related to these institutions will be included to assignments in this class will help students develop their own views on what kinds of policies can improve the functioning of public institutions. These cases will look in detail at the interplay between various public institutions and their roles in policy processes.
